name: SWOT
purpose: What is the synthesis of internal and external analysis?
apply: Weight and prioritize each factor (−5 to +5)
Keep only factors valued by customers and different from competitors
pitfalls: Using SWOT instead of a real industry and resource analysis

name: Resource-based view
purpose: Why do firms in the same industry perform differently?

parts.label: Resources vs capabilities
points: Resources = what we have (nouns): data, cash, skilled staff
Capabilities = what we do (verbs): using data, managing cash, training staff

parts.label: Tangible vs intangible
points: Tangible: capital, land, buildings, plant, equipment, supplies
Intangible: culture, knowledge, brand & reputation, IP

example: VfB Stuttgart: almost the same squad went from 16th to 2nd – capabilities (how resources are combined) beat a list of resources.

name: Value chain & value system
purpose: Which activities create value and margin – and which should be done in-house?

parts.label: Margin
points: Created by the coordinated system of activities

parts.label: Value system
points: Where to maximize quality, minimize cost → make or buy

apply: Locate the firm's key resources and capabilities in the chain
Ask which activities raise WTP and which lower cost
example: Dyson: R&D (≈50 % of net earnings), patents, direct stores and 72-hour helpdesk raise WTP; manufacturing in Malaysia lowers cost.

name: VRIO
purpose: Does a resource or capability give a sustained competitive advantage?

parts.label: V – Valuable
points: Valued by customers, lets the firm respond to opportunities/threats

parts.label: R – Rare
points: Possessed by none or few competitors

parts.label: I – Inimitable
points: Sources: causal ambiguity (“recipe”), culture & history, tacit knowledge

parts.label: O – Organized
points: Processes, structure, control, incentives to exploit it

apply: Pick specific resources from the case, not “good management”
Go through V, R, I, O with evidence and state where the chain breaks
pitfalls: VRIN → VRIO: N folded into I, O added
A resource VRIO in one industry may not be in another (Dyson in EVs)
example: Dyson in vacuums: brand, skills, innovation culture, patents = VRIO; funding = valuable only; engineers = V+R but imitable. In EVs only patents stayed VRIO → project abandoned 2019.

name: Dynamic capabilities
purpose: How does a firm stay ahead when its environment changes?

parts.label: Definition
points: Ability to renew and recreate resources and capabilities for changing environments

parts.label: Why needed
points: Advantages get imitated, become common practice or redundant

parts.label: What they do
points: Create, extend or modify the resource base
